channel.title: Winston Lin
channel.description: Case studies, writing, and practical tools on cloud platforms, developer workflows, startup advisory, operating systems, and AI-assisted work.

item.title: Clear Support Answers Build Trust
item.description: Platform PM work often comes down to a simple question: what can the customer rely on today, and what should the product team learn from the ask?

item.title: Proof points should route to evidence
item.description: A homepage stat earns more trust when it points directly to the case study, project, or note that makes the claim inspectable.

item.title: Discovery paths should name the first move
item.description: A discovery card gets easier to trust when it says what the recommended first click is instead of only naming the topic area.

item.title: Start cards should name the route
item.description: A homepage card works better when it says whether it routes to proof, context, or published work before the reader has to infer the click.

item.title: GitHub Profiles Should Keep One Context Link Per Track
item.description: A GitHub profile gets easier to trust when each repo track keeps one visible context link instead of leaving all of the explanation in a long mixed intro list.

item.title: Project Tracks Should Point to Published Work
item.description: Grouped repo tracks earn more trust when they also point to one published post or case study that shows the same preference under real constraints.

item.title: Homepages Should Offer Short Paths by Intent
item.description: A portfolio homepage gets easier to use when it offers a few opinionated routes by intent before it asks a reader to scan the larger inventory.

item.title: Alerting Starter Patterns Should Normalize Before They Notify
item.description: A starter alerting repo gets more reusable when it turns raw alert payloads into one readable message shape before the workflow hands the problem to a person.

item.title: Decision Logs Should Keep the Revisit Date Visible
item.description: A decision log stays useful when it keeps the owner, assumption, and revisit date visible enough to pull old calls back into the workflow before they turn into archaeology.

item.title: Starter Patterns Should Leave One Stable Handoff Artifact
item.description: A starter repo gets stronger when the first run leaves behind one compact artifact that a downstream system could actually consume instead of forcing every later step to re-parse the same raw input.

item.title: Docs Checks Should Point at Publish Blockers
item.description: A useful docs checker should stay close to the few issues that actually stop a draft from being ready to hand off, review, or publish.

item.title: Validation Gates Should Fail in a Useful Shape
item.description: A starter validation repo gets more reusable when the failing result is structured enough to show what broke, why it broke, and what the next fix should be.

item.title: Anchor Repos Should Carry the Batch
item.description: Once a projects page recommends one repo per track, those anchor repos need the clearest README, example, and output because they teach the standard for the rest of the batch.

item.title: Repo Tracks Should Recommend a First Example
item.description: Grouped repo tracks get much easier to read when each track names one best first example before asking a stranger to scan the full batch.

item.title: Project Pages Should Explain the Batch
item.description: A strong projects page should explain the repeated problem and standard behind a repo batch instead of flattening everything into one inventory.

item.title: Good Small Repos Should Show the Second Move
item.description: A small public repo gets more reusable when it makes the next handoff or rerun obvious instead of stopping at the first demo.

item.title: GitHub Profiles Should Choose the First Click
item.description: A good GitHub profile should make the best next click obvious instead of making a stranger sort through an undifferentiated list of links.

item.title: GitHub Should Prove and the Site Should Route
item.description: A good portfolio gets stronger when GitHub shows the proof, the site handles routing and context, and neither surface tries to do the other's job.

item.title: Repeated Work Should Become a Check
item.description: If a task keeps coming back often enough to need reminders, it usually wants a small rerunnable check instead of more memory and coordination.

item.title: Fun Projects Get Stronger When They Leave a Reusable Artifact
item.description: A small side project gets more useful when it leaves behind a clear output, handoff, or rerun path that someone can carry into real work.
